title: Deactivating a part that has a core charge also deactivates its core
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test, with a Core Charge above $0, so it has a core.
  • Make sure the Search box in the top bar is the global search, which lists inventory parts.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  2. Click Deactivate parts.
  3. Click the part A row.
  4. Click Deactivate on the dark bar.
  5. Click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  6. Click the Search box in the top bar.
  7. Type Core for followed by part A's description.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The menu opens.

Step 2:

  • Bulk mode turns on and one row is listed, for part A: its core has no row of its own, so it cannot be ticked.

Step 3:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 4:

  • The "Deactivate parts?" confirmation opens.

Step 5:

  • A green message reads "1 part updated.": only the part you ticked is counted, not its core, and no failure is listed.
  • Part A leaves the Active tab.

Step 6:

  • The global search opens.

Step 7:

  • The result for part A's core ("Core for" and part A's description) carries the grey "Inactive" tag: the core became inactive together with part A.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part), story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work)

  • S2-R17: “A part's core becomes inactive together with the part, in the same change.”
  • S10-R12a: “The counts include only the parts the user selected. A core that changes with its part is not counted, so changing 2 parts that both have a core reads "2 parts updated."”
  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
  • Feature Overview, Core functionality: “A core always has the same active state and the same tracking state as the part it belongs to.”
  • S9-R18: “Global search lists inactive parts at the current location. Each carries the grey "Inactive" tag.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
